messages:
anya: FYI release candidate rc-2026-03-1 is blocked by the security gate in canary. deploy-bot flagged a SBOM provenance mismatch for service-edge.

devon: Ugh. Is this the unsigned base-image vs customer-provided-base issue again?

anya: Looks like the builder image id changed after the rebuild. deploy-bot shows different origin checksums.

deploy-bot: Automated check failed: SBOM provenance header mismatch.

Affected artifact: service-edge:2026.03.1-canary
Detected: builder.digest != signed_provenance.digest
Action: hold canary deployment; require reviewer exception or pin base image.

sam: Can you paste the SBOM diff? small snippet is fine.

anya: ```
--- provenance.json (expected)
+++ provenance.json (observed)
@@
-    "builder": {"name": "corp-builder", "digest": "sha256:aaa111"}
+    "builder": {"name": "corp-builder", "digest": "sha256:bbb222"}
```

sec-oncall: If the digest drift is due to a rebuild that pulled a newer base patch, we need sec approval + one engineering approver. Legal only if third-party base changed.

devon: This was a quick rebuild to pick up a transitive CVE fix. I can try to pin the previous base and re-run the pipeline, but that may delay the cutover past the change window (tomorrow 10:00 PT).

anya: Change window reminder: regional cutover tomorrow 10:00 PT -> 13:00 PT. If we miss it, release goes to next window Tues.

sam: Options: 1) pin to previous base and re-run (risk: delays), 2) request exception for provenance drift with sec-oncall approval (risk: unknown provenance), 3) rollback the canary to last verified image and proceed with rest of rollout.

devon: I'm leaning to pin-and-rebuild. Pin command is in the runbook: https://go/release/runbooks/sbom-provenance-pin

anya: sec-oncall, can you review the diff quickly? If you OK an exception we need text approval in this thread mentioning @devon and @anya.

sec-oncall: Looking. Quick check shows no new external packages and the digest appears to be an internal rebuild. I can approve an exception for canary only, provided we: 1) file an incident ticket capturing the build agent change, 2) require pin for production rollout, 3) add a post-mortem if this recurs. Approving canary bypass now: APPROVE @devon @anya :white_check_mark:

devon: Thanks. I'll pin the base for prod and re-run pipelines. Can someone trigger a partial rollback for canary to last-known-good while I re-run?

deploy-bot: Received rollback request from @devon. Performing canary rollback to service-edge:2026.03.0-canary. ETA ~3m.

anya: deploy-bot: confirm when rollback complete and please attach the SBOM artifacts to ticket REL-4123.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback complete. Artifacts attached to REL-4123.

legal-ops: Noted. No third-party license changes flagged. We're good on legal for now.

sam: Great. After devon finishes the rebuild pin, let's re-run the canary and tag artifacts as signed. Keep approvals in-thread so audit shows sec decision.

anya: Filed REL-4123 and linked this thread. Closing loop: canary rolled back, sec exception granted for canary only, prod requires pinned rebuild. Move fast but safe. :thumbsup:
thread_text: release coordination thread about SBOM provenance mismatch, security exception for canary, rollback, and pin-and-rebuild plan
